label: copy-phase fed-back s early in a long recall (esp. s->p)
explanation: Very sparse feature that fires only in the copy phase, almost only when the fed-back input is s (98% of mass; p takes nearly all the rest). It fires early in the recall (recall_idx 1-3, mostly 2) and in longer sequences with many outputs left (to_go 4-7). It never fires in the original or delimiter phase, or when to_go <= 1. Magnitude is largest when the token being output after s is p (67% of mass; the top examples are s p p ... at original positions 1-2), and smaller when it is s or f. Precision is poor: copy-phase s early in a long sequence is necessary but nowhere near sufficient, because many s->p cases in shorter sequences stay silent. Best dev F1 is about 0.43 (precision 0.54, recall 0.36, mass recall 0.51). A broader predicate (fed-back s, recall_idx <= 3) reaches 0.97 recall but only 2% precision.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=s (+3.54), phase=2 & out_tok=s (+3.37), in_tok=s (+3.26), recall_idx=2 & in_tok=s (+3.15), phase=2 & out_tok=f (+3.06), orig4=o (+2.71). Lower it: correct=1 (-5.54), orig5=s (-2.43), next_out=- (-2.01), to_go=1 (-1.86).
